question.text: Scenario: Bharati Infosystems Ltd. (BIL), a listed IT company, has 2 crore outstanding equity shares with a face value of Rs.5 each. The current market price is Rs.400 per share. BIL has accumulated free reserves of Rs.500 crore and paid-up capital of Rs.10 crore. On March 1, 2025, the Board of Directors approves a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:1 (one bonus share for every one share held). The record date is set as March 15, 2025 (T Day). Naveen Sharma, the RTA officer, is responsible for processing the bonus issue. The beneficial owner download from the depository shows 15,000 individual shareholders and 200 institutional shareholders. Three months later, on June 15, 2025, BIL's Board announces a buyback of shares through tender offer at Rs.220 per share (post-bonus adjusted price), for a total buyback amount of Rs.88 crore. The record date for the buyback is July 1, 2025. Ramesh Gupta, a retail investor, holds 2,000 shares (post-bonus) with a market value of Rs.4.2 lakh on the record date. Seema Jain, another investor, holds 800 post-bonus shares with a market value of Rs.1.68 lakh on the record date. Question 3 of 5: Under the revised SEBI bonus-issue timeline, when will trading in BIL's bonus shares commence relative to the record date (T Day)?

answer.text: On T Day (same day as record date)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the revised framework, the issuer submits the required documents to the exchange by noon the next working day after T (i.e., T+1), and the bonus shares are available for trading on the T+2 day. No temporary ISIN is used; bonus shares are credited directly to the permanent ISIN. The Trap: Candidates using older material may recall longer timelines with temporary ISINs. The revised framework compressed the bonus-processing window to T+2. Note: T+1 refers to the next working day, per the workbook wording; weekends and holidays should be accounted for when mapping to calendar dates.
